In this lab, we'll practice recreating some early versions of a nice looking plot that describes how student-to-teacher ratios in primary education vary across the world.  **The process of creating a detailed, visually appealing final plot is iterative and additive**, as we will see here.  

You should be *following a similar process as you work to create your submission for the Mini Project \#1* (i.e., swapping out and layering geoms, adjusting axes to include relevant comparison points, and adding some annotations).

The data comes from [the \#TidyTuesday project](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2019/2019-05-07) and was shared on May 7, 2019.  It contains the UNESCO Institute of Statistics' country-level data on the number of teachers and teacher-to-student ratios in primary and secondary education courses (roughly, elementary and high school respectively).
Our goal will be to **describe how the variation in student-to-teacher ratios in primary schools across continents (and we want to show variability within each continent).**

I've included some lines below to read in the data.  Your job is to recreate the plots in the *Lab_5_Target_Plots.pdf* file (see the Files tab in the bottom right panel).

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Load libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggsci)


# Load the data

df_students <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2019/2019-05-07/student_teacher_ratio.csv")

# We'll also need to map each country to a continent... 
# which is not included in the `df_students` data... 
#   so let's merge on another dataset:

df_world_tile <- readr::read_csv("https://gist.githubusercontent.com/maartenzam/787498bbc07ae06b637447dbd430ea0a/raw/9a9dafafb44d8990f85243a9c7ca349acd3a0d07/worldtilegrid.csv") 
```


# Data wrangling
The chunk in this section creates the dataset you'll use in all your plots.  *Describe in words what this code chunk does.*
```{r}
df_ratios <- df_students %>% 
  filter( indicator == "Primary Education" ) %>%
  group_by(country) %>% 
  filter(year == max(year)) %>%
  inner_join( df_world_tile,
              by = join_by( country_code == alpha.3 )) 
```

This filters the students data set to courses in primary education and picks the rows with the latest year for each country. It then joins the world_tile dataset by matching the 3 character country code that is shared between the datasets. Inner join makes it so that only country codes that are in both datasets appear in the final dataset.

# Basic boxplot
```{r, eval = FALSE}

# Consider modifying the following example code:
#   ASIDE: put your modified code in its own chunk OR
#           remove the `eval = FALSE` flag on this chunk

mylabs <- labs( title = "Example title",
                caption = "Data source" )
mythemes <- theme( plot.title = element_text( 
  face = "italic", size = 20, hjust = .5 ))

ggplot(df_ratios,
       aes( x, -y, col=region) ) + 
  geom_point()
  mylabs +
  mythemes
```

```{r}
mylabs <- labs(title = "The Evolution of a ggplot",
               caption = "Data: UNESCO Institute for Statistics")
mythemes <- theme( plot.title = element_text(
  face = "bold", size = 15, hjust = .5 ))

ggplot(df_ratios) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = region, y = student_ratio)) +
  mylabs +
  mythemes
```

## A more sensible ordering

```{r}
ggplot(df_ratios) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = reorder(region, student_ratio, decreasing=TRUE), y = student_ratio)) +
  mylabs +
  mythemes
```

## Flipped axes

```{r}
ggplot(df_ratios) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = reorder(region, student_ratio, decreasing=TRUE), y = student_ratio)) +
  coord_flip() +
  mylabs +
  mythemes
```

## A relevant minimum

```{r, eval = FALSE}

# Some more example code:

ggplot(df_ratios,
       aes( x, -y, col=region) ) + 
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous( limits = c(-10,max(df_ratios$x)) ) +
  mylabs +
  mythemes
```

```{r}
ggplot(df_ratios) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = reorder(region, student_ratio, decreasing=TRUE), y = student_ratio)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,max(df_ratios$student_ratio))) +
  coord_flip() +
  mylabs +
  mythemes
```

## Color! Theme!  Better indication of the minimum!

```{r, eval = FALSE}

# Some more example code:

plot_template <- ggplot(df_ratios,
       aes( x, -y, col=region) ) + 
  #geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous( limits = c(-10,max(df_ratios$x)),
                      breaks = c(-10, seq(0,30, by=5))) +
  scale_color_uchicago() + ## from the ggsci library
  mylabs +
  mythemes

plot_template +
  geom_point()
```

```{r}
mylabs <- labs(title = "The Evolution of a ggplot",
               caption = "Data: UNESCO Institute for Statistics",
               x = "",
               y = "Student to teacher ratio")

ggplot(df_ratios) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = reorder(region, student_ratio, decreasing=TRUE), y = student_ratio, col = region)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,max(df_ratios$student_ratio))) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_color_uchicago() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  mylabs +
  mythemes
```

# Beyond the boxplot

## Distribution shapes

```{r}
ggplot(df_ratios) +
  geom_violin(aes(x = reorder(region, student_ratio, decreasing=TRUE), y = student_ratio, col = region)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,max(df_ratios$student_ratio))) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_color_uchicago() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  mylabs +
  mythemes
```

## Countries

```{r}
ggplot(df_ratios) +
  geom_point(aes(x = reorder(region, student_ratio, decreasing=TRUE), y = student_ratio, col = region)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,max(df_ratios$student_ratio)),
                     breaks = c(1, 20, 40, 60, 80)) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_color_uchicago() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  mylabs +
  mythemes
```

## Fix overplotting

```{r}
ggplot(df_ratios) +
  geom_point(aes(x = reorder(region, student_ratio, decreasing=TRUE), y = student_ratio, col = region), alpha = .3) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,max(df_ratios$student_ratio)),
                     breaks = c(1, 20, 40, 60, 80)) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_color_uchicago() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  mylabs +
  mythemes
```

## Better fix for overplotting

```{r}
ggplot(df_ratios) +
  geom_jitter(aes(x = reorder(region, student_ratio, decreasing=TRUE), y = student_ratio, col = region), alpha = .3, height = 0, width = .2) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,max(df_ratios$student_ratio)),
                     breaks = c(1, 20, 40, 60, 80)) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_color_uchicago() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  mylabs +
  mythemes
```

## Return of the boxplot

```{r}
ggplot(df_ratios, aes(x = reorder(region, student_ratio, decreasing=TRUE), y = student_ratio)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter(aes(col = region), alpha = .3, height = 0, width = .2) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,max(df_ratios$student_ratio)),
                     breaks = c(1, 20, 40, 60, 80)) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_color_uchicago() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  mylabs +
  mythemes
```

# Final tweaks

## Continental averages
```{r, eval = FALSE}

# Some more example code:

ggplot( df_ratios,
        aes( x = region,
             y = student_ratio )) +
  geom_jitter(alpha=.5) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 5)

```

```{r}
ggplot(df_ratios, aes(x = reorder(region, student_ratio, decreasing=TRUE), y = student_ratio, col = region)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = .3, height = 0, width = .2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 5) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,max(df_ratios$student_ratio)),
                     breaks = c(1, 20, 40, 60, 80)) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_color_uchicago() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  mylabs +
  mythemes
```

## World average

```{r, eval = FALSE}

# Some more example code:

world_avg <- mean(df_ratios$student_ratio)

ggplot( df_ratios,
        aes( x = region,
             y = student_ratio )) +
  geom_jitter(alpha=.5) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 5) +
  geom_segment( data = df_ratios %>%
                  group_by(region) %>%
                  summarize( student_ratio = mean(student_ratio) ),
                yend = world_avg )
```

```{r}
world_avg <- mean(df_ratios$student_ratio)

ggplot(df_ratios, aes(x = reorder(region, student_ratio, decreasing=TRUE), y = student_ratio, col = region)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = .3, height = 0, width = .2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 5) +
  geom_segment(data = df_ratios %>%
                  group_by(region) %>%
                  summarize(student_ratio = mean(student_ratio)),
                yend = world_avg) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = world_avg, linewidth = .3) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,max(df_ratios$student_ratio)),
                     breaks = c(1, 20, 40, 60, 80)) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_color_uchicago() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  mylabs +
  mythemes
```

## Annotations

```{r}
# Some helpful settings and summary statistics we'll 
#   use to annotate our plots:

annotate_text_size <- 2.5

asia_avg <- df_ratios %>% 
  filter(region == "Asia") %>% 
  pull(student_ratio) %>% 
  mean()

africa_max <- df_ratios %>%
  filter( region == "Africa" ) %>%
  pull(student_ratio) %>%
  max()

africa_min <- df_ratios %>%
  filter( region == "Africa" ) %>%
  pull(student_ratio) %>%
  min()
```


```{r}
## The base plot I'll add annotations to (for the purposes of
##    our example code below only)

plot_for_annotations <- ggplot( df_ratios,
        aes( x = reorder( region, student_ratio,
                          decreasing = TRUE ),
             y = student_ratio )) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(seed = 42), alpha=.5) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 5) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1, 90)) +
  theme_bw()
```

Choose *ONE* of the following strategies to annotate your plot:

### Option A: `geom_text`, `geom_curve`

```{r}

#
# Option A:  geom_text, geom_curve
#
#  You'll need to add this to your plot and
#     add the label for the worldwide average
#

## Code to create the details for our annotations

txt_nent <- data.frame( xstart = 2.6, ystart = 15,
                        xend = 3 -.1, yend =  asia_avg - .5,
                        labels = "Continental average ",
                        hjust = 1, vjust = .5 )

txt_tries <- data.frame( xstart = 1.3, ystart = 8,
                        xend = 1, yend = 13,
                        labels = "Countries \n per continent \n",
                        hjust = .5, vjust = 0 )
txt_tries2 <- txt_tries %>%
    mutate( xend = 1.76, yend = 18, labels = "")

txt_max <- data.frame( xstart = 1.3, ystart = 77,
                       xend = 1, yend = africa_max - 1,
                       labels = "The Central African Republic has by far\nthe most students per teacher",
                       hjust = .5, vjust = 0 )

txt_world <- data.frame( xstart = 5, ystart = 32,
                        xend = 4.5, yend =  24,
                        labels = "Worldwide average:\n23.5 students per teacher",
                        hjust = 0, vjust = .5 )

arrows_and_text <- rbind( txt_nent,
                          txt_tries, txt_tries2,
                          txt_max,
                          txt_world)


# plot_for_annotations +
# 
#     geom_text( data = arrows_and_text,
#                aes( x = xstart, y = ystart,
#                     label = labels,
#                     hjust = hjust, vjust = vjust ),
#                col = "black",
#                size = annotate_text_size ) +
# 
#     geom_curve( data = arrows_and_text,
#                 aes(x = xstart, y = ystart,
#                     xend = xend, yend = yend),
#                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.08, "inch")),
#                 size = 0.5, color = "gray20", curvature = -0.3 )
```

```{r}
world_avg <- mean(df_ratios$student_ratio)
mylabs <- labs(title = "The Evolution of a ggplot",
               caption = "Data: UNESCO Institute for Statistics",
               x = "",
               y = "Student to teacher ratio")

ggplot(df_ratios, aes(x = reorder(region, student_ratio, decreasing=TRUE), y = student_ratio, col = region)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = .3, height = 0, width = .2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", size = 5) +
  geom_segment(data = df_ratios %>%
                  group_by(region) %>%
                  summarize(student_ratio = mean(student_ratio)),
                yend = world_avg) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = world_avg, linewidth = .3) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,max(df_ratios$student_ratio)),
                     breaks = c(1, 20, 40, 60, 80)) +
  scale_color_uchicago() +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  mylabs +
  mythemes +
  coord_flip() +
  geom_text( data = arrows_and_text,
               aes( x = xstart, y = ystart,
                    label = labels,
                    hjust = hjust, vjust = vjust ),
               col = "black",
               size = annotate_text_size ) +
  geom_curve( data = arrows_and_text, 
              aes(x = xstart, y = ystart, 
                  xend = xend, yend = yend),
              arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.08, "inch")), 
              size = 0.5, color = "gray20", curvature = -0.3 )
```

### Option B: `geom_text_repel`
Note: there is some randomness in this function (just like `geom_jitter`), so it's ok if you can't match the target plot exactly.

```{r, eval = FALSE}

#
# Option B:  geom_text_repel
#
#  You'll need to add this to your plot and
#     add the label for the continental average
#

repel_pts <- tibble(
    x = c(4.5, 1.15, 1),
    y = c(world_avg, africa_max, africa_min), 
    labels = c( paste("Worldwide average:\n",
                      round(world_avg,1),
                      "students per teacher"),
                "The Central African Republic has by far
                the most students per teacher",
                "Countries\nper continent" ))


plot_for_annotations +
  
    geom_text_repel( data = repel_pts,
                     aes( x=x, y=y, label=labels ),
                     col = "black", size = annotate_text_size,
                     box.padding = 1.5, max.overlaps = Inf, 
                     nudge_y = c(15,0,0), nudge_x = c(0,.25,0),
                     min.segment.length = 0, 
                     arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.008, "npc")), 
                     segment.curvature = -.3 )

```
